title: Accounts Administration Assistant
description:
12-Month Fixed-Term Contract

A fantastic opportunity has arisen to join the finance shared services team of a highly successful global organisation operating within a fast-paced, technology-led environment.

This 12-month fixed-term position has been created to support the continued growth of the European Shared Service Centre and offers the chance to become part of a collaborative finance team supporting multiple international business entities.

The Role

As a Travel & Expense (T&E) Administrator, you will be responsible for ensuring the accurate and timely audit of employee travel and expense claims, providing support with payment activities, and delivering excellent customer service to stakeholders across the business.

Working within a dedicated team, you will help maintain compliance with company policies, resolve employee queries and contribute to the smooth operation of the wider finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Auditing travel and expense submissions in line with company policies and internal controls
- Reviewing and resolving employee and stakeholder queries relating to expenses and financial transactions
- Supporting regular payment runs across multiple entities
- Assisting with month-end and year-end finance processes
- Supporting the preparation of financial reports and documentation
- Investigating and resolving discrepancies in a timely manner
- Maintaining employee data in accordance with data protection requirements
- Working closely with colleagues and other departments to support efficient financial operations
- Contributing to process improvements, training and knowledge-sharing activities
- Supporting wider shared service centre activities as required
- Occasional travel to support finance projects and system implementations

Skills & Experience

The successful candidate will ideally possess:
- Previous experience within a transactional finance environment
- Experience using a Travel & Expense platform such as Concur, Chrome River or SAP
- ERP system experience, with SAP highly desirable
- Strong Microsoft Excel and Office skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Effective communication and stakeholder management abilities
- A proactive approach with strong problem-solving skills
- The ability to work independently and collaboratively
- A positive, customer-focused mindset

Qualifications
- Prior experience in finance administration, accounts payable or transactional finance preferred
- AAT studies or qualification would be advantageous but are not essential

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Annual bonus opportunity
- Flexible and hybrid working arrangements
- Exposure to a global finance function within a growing international organisation
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to contribute to ongoing finance transformation projects

Location

This is a hybrid position based in South Wales. Following an initial training period of approximately 12 weeks, the role will operate on a 3 days office / 2 days home working basis.

title: Warranty Administrator

description:
We are currently recruiting on behalf of our client for a highly skilled Warranty Administrator to join their reputable multi-franchise dealership in Newport. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing the warranty process across three franchises, supporting a team of five Service Advisors. This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced automotive professional seeking a long-term career with a well-established dealership group operating throughout South West England and South Wales.

Benefits for the successful Warranty Administrator:
- Salary up to £30,000 per annum, dependent on experience
- Performance-based bonus scheme
- 22 days' annual holiday plus 8 bank holidays
- Discounted car purchase programme for you and your family
- Cycle to work scheme
- Healthcare provisions and hospitality/event perks

title: Facilities Co-ordinator
description:

title: Payroll Administrator
company: Richmond Accountancy Services Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Job description:

About the role

We are looking for an experienced Payroll Administrator to join our team at Richmond Accountancy Services Limited in Abergavenny.

This is a full-time, office-based position and would suit someone who already has practical experience running payrolls and is looking to develop their career within a friendly, established accountancy practice.

You will be responsible for managing payrolls for a portfolio of clients, covering businesses of different sizes and pay frequencies.

Key responsibilities

Your role will include:
- Processing weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls
- Calculating salaries, wages, overtime, holiday pay, statutory payments and deductions
- Processing starters and leavers
- Preparing and submitting RTI returns to HMRC
- Managing workplace pension and auto-enrolment requirements
- Processing pension contributions and submissions to pension providers
- Dealing with payroll queries from clients and employees
- Preparing payroll reports, payslips and other relevant documentation
- Keeping payroll records accurate and up to date
- Ensuring payroll deadlines are met
- Liaising with HMRC and pension providers where required

Experience we're looking for

Previous hands-on payroll experience is essential. You should be comfortable managing payrolls and working to regular deadlines with a high level of accuracy.

Experience with IRIS Elements Payroll would be preferred, although this is not essential. We are very happy to consider applicants who have experience using other payroll software.

Experience dealing with workplace pensions and auto-enrolment is also important.

We're looking for someone who is organised, reliable and comfortable communicating directly with clients.

Qualifications & development

Formal payroll or accountancy qualifications are not essential if you have the right practical experience.

For someone who would like to gain further relevant professional qualifications, we are happy to support your development and fund appropriate qualifications and training.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their payroll career while gaining further qualifications alongside their role.

What we offer
- Salary of £28,000 per year
- Full-time, permanent position
- Employer-funded professional qualifications and training
- Opportunity for continued professional development
- Varied portfolio of payroll clients
- Friendly and supportive accountancy practice environment
- Office-based role in Abergavenny

Working arrangements

Job type: Full-time, Permanent

Salary: £28,000 per year

Location: Abergavenny

Work location: In person

If you have previous payroll experience and are looking for a role where you can take responsibility for client payrolls while continuing to develop your skills and qualifications, we'd be pleased to hear from you.

Apply with your CV and a brief covering note outlining your payroll experience.

title: HR Assistant
description:

Please do not apply if you have no previous HR experience in a manufacturing organisation

Hours of Work:
Monday to Thursday: 8:30am 5:00pm with a 30-minute unpaid lunch break
Friday: 8:30am 2:30pm with no lunch break

The position is 37.5 hours per week and fully site-based, with an early finish every Friday.

Key Responsibilities:
- Acting as a first point of contact for day-to-day HR queries
- Supporting the HR Manager with employee relations matters
- Assisting with reviewing and updating HR policies and procedures
- Supporting maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental leave, flexible working and other HR processes
- Monitoring absence and supporting managers with the absence management process
- Maintaining accurate employee records and updating the HR system
- Producing information and reports for payroll, production and HR
- Supporting temporary and permanent recruitment, including advertising vacancies, CV screening, interviews and onboarding
- Supporting the complete employee lifecycle, from recruitment and induction through to leavers
- Assisting with training and development administration
- Supporting performance management processes
- Helping with employee engagement, health and wellbeing initiatives
- Providing additional HR administrative support as required

The role will also provide exposure to recruitment, employee relations, capability, absence and performance management, with the opportunity to gradually take ownership of HR processes. Job Description HR Assistant

Key Requirements:
- Working knowledge of current UK employment legislation
- Experience supporting employee relations administration
- Recruitment experience
- Experience with absence management and HR processes
- Exposure to performance management administration
- Strong HR administration and record-keeping skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- High attention to detail
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information professionally
- Good organisational and interpersonal skills
- Confidence using Microsoft Office

Experience within a manufacturing environment would be beneficial but isn't essential. Experience using an HRIS would also be advantageous. A relevant HR qualification or CIPD Level 3 or above is desirable. Job Description HR Assistant.
